History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
27-year-old man with 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhoea, mid-abdominal cramping, mild nausea/vomiting, and subjective fever — clinically consistent with acute gastroenteritis; advised oral re-hydration, soft diet, paracetamol, and safety-net follow-up in 48 h.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Profuse watery diarrhoea.  
• Onset/Durations: Began ≈3 days ago (Monday/Tuesday); continues hourly while awake; not improving.  
• Character: Watery stools; no blood.  
• Associated pain: Crampy, mid-lower abdomen; colicky, precedes each bowel motion; severity ≈6/10, intermittent.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Nausea; occasional vomiting (one episode after milk ingestion).  
  – Subjective fever (“burning up”) but no temperature recorded.  
  – Mild oliguria (“passing urine less frequently”) but still voiding.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Milk triggered vomiting; otherwise none stated.  
• Triggers/exposure: Brother with similar illness × 5 days. No recent travel or takeaway food specifically recalled.  
• Oral intake: Fluids tolerated but “go straight through”; last solid meal (lunch today) passed loose.  
• Review of systems: No rectal bleeding, no persistent vomiting, no focal abdominal tenderness described; no chronic bowel disease symptoms mentioned; no other system complaints documented.

Past Medical History:
• Generally fit and well; no chronic diseases reported.  
• Medications: Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) for pain/fever.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with mother and sister; brother lives separately.  
• Employment: Office job in central London (government).  
• Smoking: Occasional social smoking (≈1 cigarette on some Fridays).  
• Alcohol: Occasional beer during weekdays; binge drinking “once or twice a month.”  
• No substance misuse disclosed.

Family History:
• Father: Colon cancer, stage III (current).  
• Brother: Recent 5-day episode of similar diarrhoeal illness (recovering).  
• No other family illnesses reported.

Physical Examination:
(No vital signs or examination findings documented in transcript.)

Investigations:
None performed or reported.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute watery diarrhoea / suspected viral gastroenteritis  
  • Likely infectious gastroenteritis given abrupt onset, high stool frequency, similar household case.  
  • Plan:  
    – Oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte) — OTC; commence immediately.  
    – Clear fluids initially, progress to bland/soft diet (soups, mashed foods) as tolerated.  
    – Continue paracetamol for pain/fever.  
    – Avoid dairy if provoking vomiting.  
    – Avoid alcohol until recovered.  
    – Safety-net: Call back/seek review if no improvement or worsening within 48 h, or signs of dehydration (reduced urine output, dizziness, inability to keep fluids down), or presence of blood in stool.

Issue 2 – Risk of dehydration  
  • High stool frequency and subjective fever raise concern.  
  • Plan: Emphasised fluid replacement, monitoring urine output; consider further assessment (bloods/IV fluids) if deterioration.

Issue 3 – Family history of colorectal cancer  
  • Not directly related to acute illness but relevant background.  
  • Plan: Documented; routine screening advice at appropriate age to be discussed at future non-urgent visit.

General plan items:  
• Provide sick note/work advice if needed.  
• Telephone follow-up in 48 h if symptoms persisting.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing expected elements: No vital signs, abdominal examination, weight, or objective hydration status recorded. Medication reconciliation limited (only paracetamol noted).  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; occasional minor audio gaps but clinical content adequate.
